answer: A port authority can require each agent to stake a refundable deposit before trading at the wharf, like a bridge toll only serious travelers pay. New identities start with low trust and earn higher limits only after verified deliveries, so spawning fake agents costs real money while yielding little. Random peer audits plus a shared reputation ledger make mass identity farming unprofitable: a yarrow seed grows slowly and cannot be bought in bulk, so rewards scale with proven history, not headcount.
